title: Rental Market Survey Data Tables, 2025 edition (October 2025 survey)
tableId: RMS 2025 tables 1.1.1 (vacancy rate) and 1.1.2 (average rent) by centre
referencePeriod: October 2025 survey (data collected early October; 2025 edition)
licence: Open Government Licence – Canada (CMHC Housing Market Information Portal, listed on open.canada.ca); CMHC website terms of use apply to site materials
attribution: Source: Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, Rental Market Survey, 2025.
transformations: Read the whole-centre row of Table 1.1.1 (Total vacancy rate) and Table 1.1.2 (average rent by Studio / 1 / 2 / 3+ bedroom) from each centre's workbook.
Numbers with thousands separators parsed to numbers; CMHC reliability code a/b/c/d kept in the note (d also flagged use_with_caution); '**' -> null + suppressed.
Ottawa and Gatineau are separate CMHC centres (Ontario part, Quebec part of CMA 505); Quebec-city value read from the 'Québec CMA' row of the Québec workbook.
notes: Universe: privately initiated apartment structures of three units and over (purpose-built rentals); rents are those charged for all units in the stock (sitting tenants and new leases), not asking rents.
CMHC publishes the next (October 2026) survey in December 2026; this is the latest available on 2026-11-04.
Brandon, Whitehorse and Iqaluit have no CMHC Rental Market Survey data table; Charlottetown and Yellowknife are covered as CAs.

title: Canadian Climate Normals 1991–2020 (station pages and composite station inventory)
publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada (Meteorological Service of Canada)
licence: Environment and Climate Change Canada data servers end-use licence / Open Government Licence – Canada
attribution: Source: Environment and Climate Change Canada, Canadian Climate Normals 1991-2020.
transformations: Station pages (results_1991_2020_e.html?climate_id=...) parsed: monthly rows for daily average/maximum/minimum temperature, precipitation and snowfall; annual 'Year' column used for totals and for days with minimum < -20 °C and maximum > 30 °C.

title: Permanent Residents - Monthly IRCC Updates: Canada - Admissions of Permanent Residents by Province/Territory and Census Metropolitan Area of Intended Destination
referencePeriod: January 2015 to August 2026 (monthly); annual totals 2015-2025; year-to-date 2026-01 to 2026-08
licence: Open Government Licence - Canada
attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada. Source: IRCC, Permanent Residents - Monthly IRCC Updates.
transformations: Read the XLSX (not the CSV, which IRCC labels 'rounded - not for calculations'); took each row's calendar-year Total column (annual totals) and the 2026 year-to-date total (January-August).

IRCC rounds every value to the nearest 5 and shows 0-5 as '--' (kept as null + suppressed flag); all values carry the 'rounded' flag. Calendar-year totals are published values and may not equal the sum of monthly cells.

Rows are 'CMA' per IRCC, which includes some census agglomerations (Charlottetown, Brandon, Whitehorse, Yellowknife are present). Ottawa - Gatineau is published as Ontario part and Quebec part and used as such.
Change = (latest-year / previous-year - 1) x 100 on rounded values; per-1,000 = admissions / StatCan July 1 population x 1000.
notes: Admissions are by intended destination at landing, not current residence.
Dataset metadata last modified 2026-10-20; file last-modified header Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:31:40 GMT.
Iqaluit: IRCC publishes Nunavut only as 'Other - Nunavut', so no Iqaluit value is available.

title: Wages (Job Bank), 2025 edition
publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada (Job Bank)
licence: Open Government Licence - Canada
attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada. Source: Employment and Social Development Canada, Job Bank Wages.
transformations: Kept NOC 2021 unit groups (5-digit), the economic regions used by our places, provinces, and Canada.
Low/median/high wage kept as published; hourly dollars unless Annual_Wage_Flag = 1 (annual dollars).
Cells with no published wage are omitted (not zero-filled); the Job Bank file refers users to the provincial/national wage in that case.
notes: Wages are of employed workers in the occupation (not advertised pay). Estimates come from the Labour Force Survey (2023-2024), Employment Insurance survey data, Small Area Estimation (2024) and, for a few occupations, the 2021 Census; the source of each cell is in the open file (Data_Source_E).
Job Bank's ER_Name differs slightly from StatCan for ER 5920 ('Lower Mainland' vs 'Lower Mainland--Southwest') and ER 6010 ('Yukon Territory' vs 'Yukon').
Territories and PEI have a single economic region equal to the territory/province; no separate provincial key is stored.
Cells kept by reference period label: {'2021': 356, '2023-2024': 10265, '2024': 5997}
Newer edition: the dataset is updated annually (previous editions 2024-12-11, 2023-12-08); re-run to pick up a 2026 edition once published (update WAGE_URL in pipeline/work/wages.py).
ER verification against our places: ER 5920: place list says 'Lower Mainland--Southwest', Job Bank says 'Lower Mainland'; ER 6010: place list says 'Yukon', Job Bank says 'Yukon Territory'

title: Market Basket Measure (MBM) thresholds for the reference family by Market Basket Measure region, component and base year

attribution: Source: Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0066-01. Reproduced and distributed on an 'as is' basis with the permission of Statistics Canada.

title: Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted
licence: Statistics Canada Open Licence
attribution: Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0004-01. Reproduced and distributed on an 'as is' basis with the permission of Statistics Canada.
transformations: 12-month % change = index(t) / index(t-12 months) - 1, rounded to 1 decimal, computed from the published index (2002=100).
Rent sub-index used: 'Rented accommodation' (city-level series exist only for this aggregate; 'Rent' alone is published for Canada and provinces only).
Places without a city series receive their province's value, flagged provincial_value.
notes: CPI is a measure of price change, not price level, and is not a cost-of-living index.
Territorial capitals are published without a Rented accommodation series (only Shelter), so cpi_rent_change_1y is not_available for Whitehorse, Yellowknife and Iqaluit; all-items is provided.

title: Mobility of immigrant taxfilers by census metropolitan areas and tax year
licence: Statistics Canada Open Licence
attribution: Source: Statistics Canada, Table 43-10-0022-01. Reproduced and distributed on an 'as is' basis with the permission of Statistics Canada.
transformations: Streamed the ~20 GB full-table CSV from the zip (not extracted) and kept Age group='Total, age group', Pre-admission experience='Total', Knowledge of official languages='Total' for Canada, provinces and our CMAs (data/raw/statcan_tables/43100022/filtered_northward.csv).

Used Statistics='Retention rate' (percent) for admission year 2018 in tax year 2023 (5 years after admission), category total; province values flagged provincial_value on place observations; CMA values as imm_retention_cma_5y.
Series: retention by years since admission for the 2015 cohort (tax years 2016-2023).
notes: 'Retention rate represents the percentage of immigrant taxfilers continuing their residence in the geographical area (province or CMA) of intended destination ... This does not take into account immigrants migrating in from another destination.' (table note 11). Retention = stayed / (stayed + out migration).
Table covers Canada, provinces and CMAs; no territories or census agglomerations.

title: Asking rent and paid rent prices, by rental unit type and number of bedrooms, experimental estimates

title: 2021 Census Cartographic Boundary Files (provinces/territories, economic regions, CMAs/CAs, census subdivisions, population centres)
licence: Statistics Canada Open Licence
attribution: Source: Statistics Canada, 2021 Census Boundary files. Reproduced and distributed on an 'as is' basis with the permission of Statistics Canada.
transformations: Read through the official StatCan GIS REST service (layers PR, ER, CMA, PC, CSD) as GeoJSON in WGS84 because the www12.statcan.gc.ca file downloads answer 403 to non-browser clients.

Provinces/territories queried one by one with identical minimal server generalization (0.0005 deg); simplified with mapshaper (topology-aware, weighted Visvalingam, keep-shapes), snapped, and densified to 0.25 deg so parallels curve under conic projection.
CMA/CA polygons for the place CMAs/CAs (Ottawa-Gatineau as its two provincial parts; Iqaluit as its CSD) simplified separately.

Economic regions overlapping each CMA/CA: each CSD in the CMA/CA assigned to the ER containing its representative point; ERs holding >= 3% of the CMA/CA population (by CSD population) are listed, the ER of the principal CSD first.
Marker: centroid (EPSG:3347) of the part of the largest population centre inside the principal CSD (representative point of the CSD if none).
notes: Cartographic (shoreline-clipped) boundaries are generalized for display; not for area measurement.
